round2.summary: Both logo walls normalize the cell box but not the ink, so marks whose source files carry wide baked-in margins render 3 to 5 times smaller than tightly cropped ones. On the sponsor wall Heads Up and Life Scientific are effectively illegible at 1440.
round2.evidence: Round 1 reported this and the fix agent declined it as belonging to the asset pass; the asset pass then fixed the four non-white grounds but not the margins, so it is still live. Measured the ink bounding box (luminance < 235) of every file in public/img/clients and public/img/sponsors with sharp, then multiplied by the wall's own 72px height cap. SPONSOR WALL rendered ink height, in a uniform cell: life-scientific 16px, harvest-returns 20px, heads-up-plant-protectants 23px, good-agriculture 31px, tidal-grow 38px, redox-bio 50px, agview-solutions 63px, nano-yield 65px, newfields-ag 70px, earthoptics 72px. A 4.5x spread. CLIENT WALL: claas 13px, south-dakota-soybean 17px, prairie-oat-growers 19px, agromark 20px, compeer-financial 20px, agfirst 21px, land-olakes-purina 22px, wilbur-ellis 24px, rising to pioneer-seeds 63px, superior-livestock 68px, california-farm-bureau 72px. A 5.5x spread. The cause is margin, not aspect ratio: ink occupies 18% of claas.png's height and 22% of life-scientific.jpg's, versus 100% of california-farm-bureau.png and earthoptics.png. The DOM confirms the boxes are already equal (all 21 client elements measure exactly 72px tall at 1440, USAEDC 38px on width). I cropped the top row of the real sponsor wall render at 1440: EarthOptics reads as a bold full-width wordmark while Harvest Returns and Heads Up sit as faint specks in identically sized cells beside it. This lands on the two deliverables the client specifically asked for, checklist lines 1 and 2, and the sponsor wall is brand-new artwork that did not exist on the old site.
round2.suggestedFix: Trim each logo to its ink bounding box in scripts/normalize-assets.mjs (the same pass that already does GROUND_FIXES and floodGroundToWhite), then re-pad to a single common ratio so the wall scales on ink rather than on canvas. Regenerate the png/webp pairs and let content/clients.ts and content/sponsors.ts pick up the new dimensions as they already do. Do not chase this in CSS: per-logo height overrides would need hand-tuning for all 31 marks and would break on the next logo drop.

round2.summary: Six of the seven generated placement comments in brand-assets.ts still name routes that do not exist, and one instructs a maintainer to reverse the wordmark to white, which is exactly what client checklist line 4 and the design system forbid.
round2.evidence:
The round-1 fix corrected one of these comments (businessOfAgriculture, which had claimed a /podcast/ masthead) but left the rest. Current file: line 16 `wordmarkWhite: '/img/brand/wordmark-white.png', // header over dark hero imagery, footer on the dark band`. docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:488 says the opposite in as many words: "Do not reverse the wordmark. wordmark-white.png exists in the asset library and this system does not use it." The build currently obeys the design system (76 wordmark references across all 19 pages, every one wordmark.png, zero wordmark-white), so this is a latent instruction to break a checklist line, not a live breach.

The other five name routes that do not exist. The app has no /the-granary/ and no /podcast/ (the hub is /podcasts/), yet: `granary: … // /the-granary/ hero`; `xtremeAg: … // /the-granary/ and /podcast/`; `businessOfAgricultureLockup: … // /podcast/ alternate lockup`; `businessOfAgricultureIconWhite: … // /podcast/ leaf icon`; `businessOfAgricultureAvatar: … // /podcast/ square avatar`; and in brandAssetsExtra `xtremeAgTransparent: … // /the-granary/`. The real placements are /xtreme-ag/ and /the-business-of-agriculture/. These strings are emitted by scripts/normalize-assets.mjs lines 667, 672, 673, 683, 684 and 685, so editing content/brand-assets.ts alone would be reverted by the next asset run.

Related gap in the same bookkeeping: `boasg-white-flat.jpg` is the client's own supplied BOASG-BRAND-LOGO-FINAL-WHITE.jpg, is referenced by no route, and has no row in the deliberately-dropped table in docs/CONTENT_MANIFEST.md, unlike the five photographs the round-1 fix did document. No content is actually lost here, I opened both files and the artwork is pixel-identical to the boasg-white.png badge already rendering at 410x410 on /boasg/, but it is the one supplied asset with no written disposition.
round2.suggestedFix: Fix the comment strings at their source in scripts/normalize-assets.mjs (lines 667, 672, 673, 683, 684, 685) and regenerate, so they name real routes. For wordmarkWhite, replace the placement claim with the rule, something like "not used: the wordmark never reverses, see DESIGN_SYSTEM section 9 rule 4". Add one row to the dropped table in docs/CONTENT_MANIFEST.md recording that boasg-white-flat.jpg is a duplicate of the badge already shown on /boasg/.

round2.summary: The three demo-reel posters are still fetched eagerly at Medium priority for a video grid 6.5 screens below the fold, because the poster attribute is on the server-rendered
round2.evidence: Controlled A/B on the production server at :3200, mobile, 3 runs each: baseline 90/90/90 with LCP 3.531s / 3.531s / 3.532s; with `*/img/video-posters/*` blocked 93/93/92 with LCP 3.156s / 3.158s / 3.307s. So the posters alone are worth 3 points and 0.373s. Lighthouse's network list for /keynote/ mobile shows them at Medium priority, above every lazy image on the page: `Image Medium 6271 /img/video-posters/dm-food-waste.webp`, `Image Medium 18174 /img/video-posters/dm-labor.webp`, `Image Medium 15414 /img/video-posters/dm-innovation.webp` = 39,859 B, fetched after the hero portrait and BEFORE the Source Serif italic. Measured with Playwright at 412x823: the three .dm-video__stage elements start at y=5324, 5653 and 5983 in a 12,027px document, i.e. the first one is 6.5 viewports down. MECHANISM, and it has changed since round 1: a components-area fix has since given the MP4 branch the same facade the YouTube branch uses, so `` now exists and would not fetch anything this far below the fold. But the server render is `hydrated === false`, so the facade is not emitted and the bare `
round2.suggestedFix: Stop paying for the no-JS still on the JS path. Render the facade unconditionally and move the bare `<video controls poster=...>` into a `<noscript>` block, so the poster bytes are never parsed when JavaScript is on and the no-JS guarantee the component's header comment protects is unchanged. Attach the real `<video>` on activation, which the component already does through `activated`. If `<noscript>` is unacceptable, the cheaper half-measure is to drop `poster` from the server-rendered `<video>` entirely: no-JS visitors then get a black frame with native controls instead of a still, and the 40KB and 0.37s come back. Fix it in VideoEmbed.tsx so /collaboration-opportunities/ is covered by the same change, and re-run scripts/lighthouse.mjs, which already audits both routes.

round2.summary: The LCP image on every route where an image is LCP carries no priority hint, so Lighthouse's lcp-discovery-insight scores 0. Next 16's `priority` prop only emits a preload link and no longer sets fetchPriority, which is the assumption Header.tsx's own comment records but Hero.tsx never acts on.
round2.evidence: lcp-discovery-insight on /acres-tv/ mobile scores 0 with the checklist `priorityHinted: false, requestDiscoverable: true, eagerlyLoaded: true`, naming `section#acres-tv > figure.dm-hero__figure--band > div.dm-hero__media > img.dm-photo__img` (microphones-background.jpg, 412x854). Same 0 on /keynote/, /about/ and /speaking/ desktop, where the hero portrait is LCP. Root cause is in the installed Next: node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/get-img-props.js:587 maps `priority` to `preload: only`, and `fetchPriority` is a separate prop threaded through getDynamicProps() at node_modules/next/dist/client/image-component.js:120-133. Neither Hero.tsx call site passes it, so no `` on the site emits fetchpriority and neither does the preload link. Header.tsx:100-112 already states the intent ('if Next starts honouring it with a real priority hint we want that hint on the hero portrait alone') and Hero.tsx is where that would have to happen. I did NOT take this on the audit's word: I built a variant with `fetchPriority="high"` added to both Hero call sites, served it on :3301, and ran a paired A/B against :3200, 3 runs per cell. The audit flips 0 -> 1 on all four routes that fail it, and the measured effect is small: /keynote/ desktop LCP 803ms -> 712ms (median, 3/3 consistent), /acres-tv/ mobile 3361ms -> 3365ms (no change), /about/ and /speaking/ desktop unchanged, and no category score moved anywhere. So this is a real audit failure and a real missing hint on a real LCP element, worth about 0.09s at best under Lantern's simulation, and plausibly more on a real congested link where a priority hint actually reorders the queue.
round2.suggestedFix: Add `fetchPriority="high"` alongside `priority={image.priority ?? true}` at both Hero.tsx <Image> sites (the portrait at line 194 and the band at line 228), and update the Header.tsx comment, which currently says neither form emits the hint, to say that Hero now passes it explicitly and the masthead deliberately does not. Do not add it to the wordmark: it is LCP on no route in either form factor. Verify by re-running scripts/lighthouse.mjs and checking lcp-discovery-insight is 1 on /acres-tv/ mobile and on /keynote/, /about/, /speaking/ desktop.

round2.summary: image-delivery-insight in Lighthouse 13.4.1 compares file pixels against CSS pixels and ignores the emulated device pixel ratio, so its 'larger than it needs to be' rows are false under Lighthouse's own mobile emulation. The runner reports it as a >0.2s opportunity with no caveat, and round 1 acted on it once already.
round2.evidence: Ran /keynote/ mobile at deviceScaleFactor 1, 1.75 and 3 and compared what the insight says about dm-labor.webp, which is a plain with no srcset so the same 640x360 file is used at every DPR. All three runs report the identical string: 'This image file is larger than it needs to be (640x360) for its displayed dimensions (370x208).' 370x208 is the CSS box. At DPR 1.75 the device box is 648x364 and at DPR 3 it is 1110x624, i.e. the 640x360 file is correctly sized at 1.75 and UNDERSIZED at 3, yet the insight calls it oversized in both. At DPR 3 it also flags the wordmark as '640x159 for its displayed dimensions (160x40)', a 4x error that is exactly the DPR. The trace-engine code carries the warning itself: node_modules/@paulirish/trace_engine/models/trace/handlers/ImagePaintingHandler.js:113-118 says 'Painting in Chrome never uses the emulated DPR... the displayed size unexpectedly ignores any emulated DPR and so the results may be very misleading', and the correction only runs when metadata.hostDPR is present and differs. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE, rather than being trivia: this insight was the primary evidence in the round-1 poster finding, the fix agent resized the posters to 640x360 on its recommendation and recorded that it verified the insight had cleared, and it has not cleared. It currently reports score 0, 150ms and 51,885 B on /keynote/, naming the same dm-labor.webp and dm-innovation.webp plus the hero portrait at w=750, all three of which are correctly sized for DPR 1.75. Following it again would mean shrinking the posters to 370x208 and the hero portrait to 370x554, which would be visibly soft on every retina phone. The 150ms LCP saving it advertises on /keynote/ is phantom; the real poster cost is 373ms and is finding 1, measured by blocking rather than by insight.
round2.suggestedFix: Add a note to the opportunities() comment block in scripts/lighthouse.mjs saying that image-delivery-insight's useResponsiveSize rows are DPR-blind under emulation and must be confirmed by a blocking A/B before anyone resizes an asset, citing the DPR 1/1.75/3 result above. Optionally have opportunities() tag rows from that audit id as unverified so they do not read the same as render-blocking-insight. Do not resize public/img/video-posters/*.webp or the hero portraits: at the 1.75 DPR Lighthouse emulates, 640x360 and w=750 are the correct picks.
